chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated from Ibn Miskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Islam began as something strange and will return as something strange as it began, so good news for the strangers. I said: Explain this to me, may God rectify you. He said: From what the caller among us will initiate anew is a new call, just as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) called.

key_terms.الدَّاعِي: The caller (referring to the Imam/Qa'im calling to God)
key_terms.الغُرَبَاءُ: The strangers (those who hold fast to Islam when it becomes rare or unfamiliar)
key_terms.جَدِيدًا: New (referring to the renewal of the call/mission)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith 'Islam began strange and will return strange' mean in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the Prophet’s hadith on Islam’s strangeness as a reference to the Qa'im (the Awaited Imam) launching a renewed, distinct call to God that mirrors the initial prophetic mission. This interpretation highlights the eschatological role of the Imam in restoring pure monotheism amidst societal deviation, a concept central to Twelver Shia eschatology. The 'strangers' are thus those who maintain fidelity to the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings during the period of occultation and beyond.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (2) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah bin Younus narrated from Muhammad bin Ja’far al-Qarashi from Muhammad bin al-Husayn bin Abul Khattab from Muhammad bin Sinan from ibn Miskan from Abu Baseer that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“Islam has begun strange and it will return strange as it has begun. Blessed are the strangers!” Abu Baseer said to him: “Please, explain to me what this means!” He said: “Al-Qa’im will invite to a new mission as the Prophet (S) has done.” The same was narrated by Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah from the previous narrators from Muhammad bin Sinan from al-Husayn bin al-Mukhtar from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as).
